source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Durham campus holds 40 MW of published IT capacity, which is 80 percent of all the data center capacity North Carolina has disclosed.

Nineteen data center facilities are mapped in the state. Only five publish megawatt figures, and fourteen publish none. So the state's disclosed inventory is essentially this one campus plus four smaller disclosures, and the real total is unknown. Disclosure here is a choice operators make, not a measurement anyone takes.

Megawatts of IT capacity are the closest public proxy for how much compute a site can host, which is why the concentration matters. But the operator publishes no certifications, no power infrastructure, no PUE, no grid operator, and no power purchase agreements. Without those, 40 MW is a nameplate figure rather than a statement about continuous load. The accelerator estimate, roughly 1,280 chips at 100 kW per rack and 40 kW per GPU, is arithmetic on assumed densities, not an operator disclosure.

Nothing in the data breaks capacity down by workload or tenant class, so it cannot distinguish general-purpose colocation from AI training. The suitability score of 69 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion missing. The data also does not cover construction dates, peak draw, or whether the grid serving Durham can supply this load.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
